product.olivetti-pcs42p-d2-50.summary: The entry to the PCS42P Enhanced platform, in a compact case with fewer expansion positions.
product.olivetti-pcs42p-d2-50.history: The PCS42P D2/50 belonged to the PCS range for personal use, study and entertainment, as described in MCmicrocomputer 137 (February 1994, p. 176). Olivetti included it in the same modular line as the M4-4xx, with the Enhanced platform and compact SLIM TIN BOX case; the PCS42P D2/50 E offered the other case. A Gladrags review (February 1996), preserved as a reproduction, shows a PCS42P with educational software and games without identifying its CPU variant. Identity sources: Pocket Service Guide, pp. 4-1–3.
product.olivetti-pcs42p-d2-50.warning: Historical research sheet; no creation profile or validation of this commercial model in BluMach.
The case and board distinguish this configuration from its siblings. The manual identifies PCS42P D2/50 as XSS42 D250, with a Enhanced board, a 50 MHz CPU and a 25 MHz bus. In its table, S identifies the compact M4 case and E the large PCS42P case; E does not mean Entry.

RAM expands through two modules. The guide supports 4–64 MB in two 70 ns SIMM banks: 4/8/16/32 MB modules with parity or 4/8 MB without parity, including mixed populations. It provides for 128 or 256 KB L2 cache; standard installation is not assumed.

Case size determines how many cards fit. The IN2025 riser offers 3 positions: two shared ISA/VESA and 1 ISA; the motherboard also provides an AT connection for audio. The guide specifies a 100 W power supply (pp. 4-2–3).

The BIOS can be updated from floppy disk. The manual lists revisions 1.09–1.11 and calls the 28F001BX ‘1 MB’ (pp. 4-7 and 4-10); Intel specifies 1 Mbit, 128K × 8, or 128 KiB (290406-007, p. 1). These are different units; retaining the manual’s wording does not endorse that capacity.

No firmware set is confidently assigned to this Enhanced configuration. The 128 KiB dump preserved as BA2142 has an Entry attribution; sharing a commercial family does not demonstrate that it can be used here.

The manual’s configurations have been cross-checked and preserved files verified. BluMach includes the experimental olivetti_ba2142 board targeting Entry; this does not validate the 26 commercial configurations or establish equivalence with Enhanced.

This model cannot yet be created from the sheet. Its board and ROM set need identification, followed by validation of boot, RAM, video, keyboard, CMOS, disks and resets. The BA2142 baseline uses a chipset approximation and read-only Flash; its code also disagrees between a UMC label and an OPTi device. No dump execution test or new antivirus scan has been performed.
Olivetti, Personal Computer — Pocket Service Guide, M4-4x4/M4-4x2/PCS42P chapter, pp. 4-1–7, 4-10 and 4-13: identity, architecture and revisions; discrepancies retained.
Paolo Ciardelli, ‘Olivetti M4-62 Modulo’, MCmicrocomputer 137, February 1994, p. 176: positioning of the M4, PCS and M6 ranges; the M4-62 price is not transferred.
Intel, 1-Mbit Boot Block Flash Memory, 290406-007, November 1995, p. 1: 28F001BX capacity; the date belongs to the document, not the computer.
BluMach 88f74ba3, machine_table.c and m_at_socket1.c: experimental BA2142 platform, code comparison without validation of this model.

Enhanced expands video and adds local-bus IDE. The guide specifies CL-GD5428 with 1–2 MB and 82C611; for I/O it says SMC37C655 on pp. 4-3 and 4-7, but SMC37C665 in the notes on pp. 4-5–6. It also classifies BA2133 as Enhanced on p. 4-2 and Entry on p. 4-6. Both readings are retained without assigning a specific board to the model.
Gladrags, February 1996, PCS42P clipping reproduced by Soumyadip Choudhury in Cutting the Chai (2008). No CPU identified; its 74,195-rupee price is not assigned to this variant.
